description.narrative: This indicator is taken from the MFA Result Framework Security and Rule of Law (Annual Plan 2020)

comment.narrative: This indicator is connected to our CSO Accelerator activities and impact of the supported CSOs.

A total of 1,274 beneficiaries gained improved access to justice through various program activities. Key achievements include community forums on land rights, training sessions for women, and direct legal assistance, particularly in securing land rights. Community leaders were trained in dispute resolution, and women received information sessions on their legal rights. While the program successfully addressed land rights, specific data on women presenting cases of sexual violence or domestic abuse is not available as none of the CSOs specifically focus on cases of sexual violence and/or domestic abuse.

title.narrative: Niger Logframe
Number of people whose justice issues are potentially prevented or resolved by supported justice service providers in Niger, after receiving an investment

comment.narrative: Mid-term evaluation performed by independent evaluators. This mid-term data point represents the initial measurement for this impact indicator. A comparative analysis will be conducted during the program's final year to assess changes and progress, acknowledging the absence of an established baseline for this evaluation.

Building upon observations, stakeholder dialogues, and beneficiary feedback, the mid-term evaluation confirms that the project significantly improved beneficiaries' legal knowledge and ability to address justice issues. Training sessions, awareness campaigns, and community engagement, particularly through traditional leaders, contributed to an 80% agreement among respondents that their understanding of rights and procedures had enhanced. This empowerment led to increased citizen-driven dispute resolution. However, 10-15% expressed reservations, indicating persistent challenges in reaching vulnerable populations and ensuring accessible information delivery. Regional disparities and resource limitations remain, necessitating continued efforts to expand legal education and strengthen citizen capacity. This mid-term data, the first of its kind, will be compared to final-year results, despite the absence of a baseline, to assess progress.

title.narrative: Niger logframe
the % of people (f/m) who declare having confidence in the competent judicial institutions (formal/informal) and dealing with their justice needs in a fair, impartial and effective manner

comment.narrative: Mid-term evaluation performed by independent evaluators. This mid-term data point represents the initial measurement for this impact indicator. A comparative analysis will be conducted during the program's final year to assess changes and progress, acknowledging the absence of an established baseline for this evaluation.

Based on the mid-term evaluation, which utilized observation, stakeholder dialogues, and beneficiary feedback, approximately 70% of beneficiaries express increased trust in the competence and effectiveness of both formal and informal judicial institutions to address their justice needs fairly and impartially. This reflects a positive trend attributed to project-supported dialogues and judicial training, leading to a greater acceptance of formal processes and perceived impartiality. However, a significant 20% of respondents voiced partial or complete distrust, highlighting persistent challenges such as resource availability and procedural delays. While the evaluation indicates improved institutional responsiveness and equity, access to justice remains uneven, particularly for remote and marginalized populations, necessitating continued efforts to strengthen confidence and ensure equitable service delivery.

title.narrative: Niger Programme Logframe

comment.narrative: This indicator is connected to our 'enabling environment' activities mainly the Stakeholder Dialogue.

While no formal law or policy reforms were directly attributable to the project during the 2024 reporting period, the program has actively engaged in foundational activities that are crucial precursors to such advancements. These include fostering dialogue with judicial authorities, providing training on enhanced judicial practices, strengthening access to justice, building the capacity of local actors, and promoting fairer practices. These efforts are designed to create an environment conducive to future legal and policy changes, and it is anticipated that the impact of these activities may manifest in tangible reforms during the next reporting period.

title.narrative: Niger Programme Logframe
# of (updated) justice needs and outcomes data sets collected

comment.narrative: One justice needs survey was conducted. Instead of a full report, results were disseminated via factsheets and an interactive dashboard. While a full Justice Needs Satisfaction (JNS) report was initially planned, it was determined, with donor approval, that the data was largely consistent with the previous year's findings. To ensure more targeted dissemination and efficient use of resources, the project shifted its focus to developing factsheets on key findings and creating an interactive data dashboard. This approach allowed for broader reach and easier access to the data for various stakeholders.

title.narrative: Niger Programme Logframe

II.a # of justice institutions/organizations adopt guideline based on the co-created implementation plan (also indicate # of justice practitioners working in the concerned field in these institutions/organizations)

comment.narrative: This indicator is connected to our CSO Accelerator activities and impact of the supported CSOs.

This indicator is met through the program's strategic focus on empowering local CSOs to enhance justice mechanisms. The 3 CSO organisations were provided with training and coaching in areas such as project management, communication, and tailored solution development, enabling them to effectively address local justice needs. The strengthening of these CSOs directly contributes to the enhancement of justice institutions by improving their operational capacity and community engagement. Furthermore, the 11 trained leaders, and the 20 community leaders, who's skills were strengthened to support local justice dynamics, also contributed to the strengthening of local justice institutions
